title: Diagonal language time bound
statement: Let $W$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and output, and let $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible. The language consisting of words $x$ for which $W$ does not halt at time $g(|x|)$ with output the single bit $1$ is decidable in time $c\bigl(g(n)+1\bigr)$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$.
hypotheses_covered: W is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
